name: Tower Semiconductor

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Tower Semiconductor.svg, served from commons.wikimedia.org)

description: Tower is a specialty chip foundry: it manufactures analog, RF, power, image-sensor and silicon photonics chips designed by fabless chip companies and by device makers, rather than competing on leading-edge digital transistors. It runs fabs in Israel, California, Texas and Japan (51% of a joint company with Nuvoton) and shares a 300 mm fab in Italy with STMicroelectronics. Customers pay per wafer, and for the fast-growing silicon photonics and silicon-germanium lines serving AI data-center optical links, some customers are now prepaying to reserve capacity through 2028 while Tower spends about $920 million to expand it. Revenue was $1,566 million in 2025 and the operating margin was 12.4%; the largest single customer, Nuvoton's Japanese unit (also Tower's partner in the Japan fabs), was 11%.

hq.note: Ramat Gavriel Industrial Park, Migdal Haemek (FY2025 20-F); fabs also in the US, Japan and Italy

employees.note: 1,296 in Israel, 1,586 in the United States, 2,398 in Japan and 36 elsewhere; 430 in R&D, 59 with PhDs (FY2025 20-F; total is the sum of the stated locations, matching the table total)

businessLines.name: Silicon photonics (SiPho) and SiGe BiCMOS for AI data-center optical links
businessLines.how: Wafers sold per unit to optical-chip designers, with some customers prepaying in 2026 for reserved capacity through 2028; prepayments are credited against their future purchases.
businessLines.description: SiPho chips for optical transceivers (200 mm PH18 and 300 mm PH45 platforms, ramping a 1.6 Tb/s platform) and SiGe BiCMOS for high-speed optical and copper networking, automotive radar and RF.
businessLines.revenueNote: Not reported by technology; the 20-F says a significant amount of 2025 revenue came from its target specialized technologies (RF CMOS including RF SOI, SiGe BiCMOS, SiPho, power ICs, discrete devices and CMOS image sensors) together.

businessLines.name: RF CMOS and RF SOI
businessLines.how: Wafers sold per unit to fabless RF chip companies and module makers, with volumes tied to handset and connectivity cycles.
businessLines.description: Antenna switches, front-end modules and transceivers for smartphones, IoT and infrastructure, at 0.18 micron, 0.13 micron and 65 nm.

businessLines.name: Power management, mixed-signal, CMOS image sensors and other analog
businessLines.how: Wafers sold per unit across consumer, industrial, automotive, medical and aerospace-and-defense customers; milestone payments for helping third parties build or ramp fabs, sometimes with capacity-allocation rights.
businessLines.description: Power ICs and discretes (including BCD and 700V), CMOS image sensors, non-imaging sensors, MEMS, mixed-signal and displays; also process-transfer and design-enablement services.

brands.name: Tower Partners Semiconductor Co. (TPSCo), Japan
brands.segment: 51% owned (Nuvoton Technology Corporation Japan holds 49%); operates the Uozu and Tonami fabs
brands.share: Revenue share not stated; NTCJ, its other owner, is also Tower's largest customer at 11% of 2025 revenue

brands.name: Tower Semiconductor Newport Beach (Fab 3, California) and Jazz Semiconductor Trusted Foundry
brands.segment: Wholly owned; includes silicon photonics and a trusted-foundry unit for US defense work

brands.name: Tower Semiconductor San Antonio (Fab 9, Texas)
brands.segment: Wholly owned; acquired from Maxim in 2016

brands.name: Fab 2 (Migdal Haemek, Israel) and Fab 10 (Agrate, Italy, shared with STMicroelectronics)
brands.segment: Fab 2 is the Israeli production fab (Fab 1 stopped operating in 2025); Tower uses about one-third of the Agrate 300 mm clean room
brands.share: Capacity by site not stated in the text read
